series_key: using the mql5 economic calendar for news filtering
mechanism: For each cached MQL5 calendar event that passes importance and currency gates, define windowStart = eventTime − NewsMinutesBefore*60 and windowEnd = eventTime + NewsMinutesAfter*60. If TimeCurrent() is inside [windowStart, windowEnd], treat the market as inside an active news-restricted regime (IsNewsTime/isUpcomingNews true). Pre- and post-buffers are inputs (default 5 min each) so the regime spans pre-release anticipation plus post-release instability, not only the release tick.
data_needed: MqlCalendarValue[] via CalendarValueHistory over rolling now→now+24h; CalendarEventById for name/importance; TimeCurrent(); NewsMinutesBefore/After
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, GBPJPY, AUDUSD, GOLD, US100 examples; FX pairs + indices/metals/commodities via currency heuristics; window in minutes around scheduled event (not bar TF); 24h calendar horizon
why_new_for_mis: Turns broker economic calendar into a discrete scheduled news-regime sensor with configurable pre/post buffers—MIS can label news-active vs normal periods without HTTP scrapers.
quote: The news filter does not react only to the exact release time of an event. Instead, it defines a configurable buffer window around the event to account for pre-release volatility and post-release market instability.

series_key: using the mql5 economic calendar for news filtering
mechanism: Derive symbol currencies via GetRelevantCurrencies: 6-letter FX → base+quote substrings; keyword heuristics map GER/DE40/DAX→EUR, UK/FTSE→GBP, US30/DJ/SPX/US500/NAS/US100/XAU/GOLD/XAG/SILVER/OIL/WTI/BRENT→USD, JPN/NIK→JPY, plus AUD/CAD/NZD/CHF/EUR/GBP/JPY name hits; optional SymbolCurrencyOverride CSV. Map each calendar event to currency via CalendarCountryById(ev.country_id).currency. Event is relevant only if event currency equals one of the symbol’s currencies—irrelevant currencies never activate the news regime.
data_needed: chart/traded symbol name; optional SymbolCurrencyOverride; MqlCalendarEvent.country_id; CalendarCountryById → country.currency
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD (EUR,USD), GBPJPY (GBP,JPY), GOLD/XAU→USD, US100→USD, GER40/DAX→EUR, FTSE→GBP, oil→USD, NIK→JPY; any broker symbol with override
why_new_for_mis: Currency-aware impact routing lets MIS attribute calendar shocks only to instruments that share the event currency instead of globally blanketing all symbols.
quote: An economic event is considered relevant if its currency matches at least one of the symbol's associated currencies.

series_key: using the mql5 economic calendar for news filtering
mechanism: While scanning TodayEvents[], load MqlCalendarEvent and gate on NewsImportanceMode: NEWS_HIGH_ONLY (CALENDAR_IMPORTANCE_HIGH), NEWS_MODERATE_ONLY, or NEWS_HIGH_AND_MODERATE. Only matching importance levels can open a news window. Combined with the time buffer, this is a severity-filtered scheduled-volatility anticipator—the article frames major releases as causing spikes, spread expansion, slippage, and SL-hunting wicks. Calendar cache reloads only when never loaded or older than CacheReloadHours (default 6).
data_needed: ev.importance from CalendarEventById; NewsImportanceMode enum; TodayEvents[] cache; CacheReloadHours; lastCalendarLoad
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: same multi-asset set as currency gate; high/moderate/red/yellow calendar tiers; rolling 24h load, ~6h refresh
why_new_for_mis: Importance-tiered native-calendar filter gives MIS a broker-local leading indicator of expected abnormal volatility windows without measuring realized vol from ticks.
quote: During major economic releases, the market often experiences: sudden price spikes, spread expansion, slippage, stop-loss hunting wicks.

series_key: using the mql5 economic calendar for news filtering
mechanism: On each tick under EnableNewsFilter, compute currentNewsState = IsNewsTime(_Symbol) and compare to static lastNewsState. When they differ: rising edge (false→true) = news window started; falling edge (true→false) = news window ended. Transitions fire once per edge (not every tick inside the window), driving one-shot risk actions. Part 2 uses this change sensor to suspend/restore SL/TP; Part 1’s latch is replaced by the same start/end model.
data_needed: IsNewsTime(_Symbol) boolean; static lastNewsState; EnableNewsFilter; OnTick evaluation
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: single-symbol EA on chart _Symbol (explicit multi-symbol limitation); news window minutes from Part 1; event-driven not bar TF
why_new_for_mis: Explicit edge detection on calendar regime occupancy yields clean regime-change events (enter/exit news stress) MIS can timestamp and join to other sensors.
quote: If those two values differ, a transition occurred. The transition is either news just started or news just ended.

series_key: using the mql5 economic calendar for news filtering
mechanism: Part 2 does not measure spread from the book; it treats the Part-1 restricted news window as a proxy for abnormal liquidity conditions—widened spreads, transient spikes, temporary distortions that trip SL/TP early. The sensing signal remains IsNewsTime; the article’s rationale maps that Boolean onto expected liquidity/execution degradation during high-impact releases, recommending short windows (e.g. 3–10 minutes) because exposure without hard stops is intentional only while that stress is presumed.
data_needed: IsNewsTime from Part 1 calendar pipeline; SuspendStopsDuringNews flag; broker SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL only at restore time (not for sensing)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: chart _Symbol single-symbol; magic-filtered positions; short news windows ~3–10 min recommended
why_new_for_mis: Frames scheduled calendar windows as an anticipatory liquidity-stress label MIS can fuse with actual spread sensors later, without claiming directional prediction.
quote: trades opened before the news window still experience widened spreads, transient spikes, and temporary distortions that can trigger SL/TP levels prematurely.
